title: Nonuniqueness for the periodic hard-sphere Boltzmann equation

issues.location: Sec 7 (eq. rescaling) / Sec 8 l>0 case / Prop 9.1
issues.description: In the separation sequence, s_N/T_N -> 0 means that any limit with l>0 has U = lim (T/s)(s/r) = infinity. So the l>0 branches of Prop. nonzero-limit are only ever used to feed the branching contradiction; in effect, Prop. finite-dilated-horizon forces l=0. The logic is consistent, but the paper never says this, and a reader may think l>0 with finite U is a live case.
issues.evidence: U_N = T_N/r_N = (T_N/s_N)(s_N/r_N) -> infinity * l when l>0.

coverage:
Read in full: introduction, framework/admissibility definition, Sec 5 (cap selection), Sec 7 (dilation), Sec 8 (nonconcentration), Sec 9 (branching), Sec 10 (separation), and most of Sec 6 (fixed-horizon limits, entropy, DiPerna–Lions/Levermore–Masmoudi continuation). In Sec 3, read the sheet-class definition, the sheet gain bound and the kernel-tightness statements; checked the G_d tilt constant 46. Sec 4 (cold-jet control) was taken on trust, along with the proofs of the remaining Sec 3 lemmas (kernel-tightness, Gaussian parameter tails, quadratic gain bound).

Computations checked:
- Cap: the D t^A supersolution and the λ* endpoint/connectedness argument.
- Five-gain iteration: the (C log(t/a))^j/j! bound and the residual.
- Two-axial-gain mismatch: the order-of-choices argument, including the identity ξ3 − z2/t2 = (t1/t2)(ξ3 − z1/t1).
- Rank-7 witness at equal times: orthogonality of k1, k2, k3, k4 to their normals; det = X²+Y²; block-triangular minor.
- Uniform pullback lemma.
- Branching: child speed law (s+1+RZ)/2, exit probability ≤ 1/26, constants c0 = 48π/13 and C0 = 48π, Markov reweighting W = (2p−1)ν0, sphere-map derivative (e1+3e3)/4, density-ratio scaling, and growth 3^n against (1+a)^{4n}.
- Dormant-vanishing bound and the diagonal dilation inequality r^{-1}h ≤ ρ^{-1} f(ρ·).
- Q+ ≤ 2Q− + (8/log 2)D.
main_claim: There is a periodic hard-sphere datum F0 with bounded velocity support and finite mass, energy and absolute entropy that has two distinct global admissible solutions: renormalized, with local mass and total momentum conservation and the energy and entropy-dissipation inequalities. On a common initial interval both are strongly L^1-continuous and have integrable gain and loss. The proof compares a dormant family, which has no hot seed, with a family of cap-saturating seeded approximations. A dilation around the cap hit gives a nonzero linear-Boltzmann limit in a two-beam background (by nonconcentration). Branching growth forces a finite dilated horizon, and this contradicts the vanishing of the dilated dormant limit.
sibling_notes: This is the 'OpenAIPeriodic' companion. The rank-365 sibling (local-conservation variant) took its dilation, nonconcentration and branching sections (9–11 there) on trust. I checked the corresponding Secs 7–9 here in detail and found no gap, which closes much of that trust dependency. The kernel/cold lemmas in Secs 3–4 were only partly reviewed.
